# Blazor

- BLZ-002: Generally, avoid creating components that write directly to their own component parameters. Component parameters should be declared as auto properties, with no custom logic in their get or set accessors. Don't use the required modifier or an init accessor on component parameter properties.
- BLZ-004: Avoid thread-blocking calls in components. When a component must be updated from an external event, such as a timer or other notification, use InvokeAsync to dispatch the work to Blazor's synchronization context.
- BLZ-005: Always unsubscribe event handlers from .NET events, and always dispose objects a component creates on the .NET side to avoid leaking managed memory.
- BLZ-007: Avoid creating a single large class that represents the entire global application state; prefer granular classes cascaded separately, each with specific subscriptions, so only the components that use a portion of the state are affected when it changes.
- BLZ-010: When adopting server-side rendering, JS interop calls must be asynchronous, and for server-side components the asynchronous invokeMethodAsync is recommended over the synchronous invokeMethod. In server-side apps with server interactivity, JS interop may fail due to networking errors and should be treated as unreliable.
- BLZ-011: In interactive server-side Blazor, the app must include appropriate checks and limits before performing potentially CPU-intensive work, and, as a general recommendation, clients shouldn't be permitted to allocate an unbounded amount of memory. Always validate data when handling events, don't trust calls from JavaScript to .NET methods, and don't make authorization decisions based on the state of the UI, only from component state.
- BLZ-012: Rendering raw HTML constructed from any untrusted source should always be avoided, and so should rendering HTML content directly from a database. Avoid passing user-supplied data in parameters to JavaScript calls; for example, don't write user-supplied data to the DOM by setting an element's innerHTML property. Avoid using user input as part of navigation call arguments.
- BLZ-018: Don't directly inject a scoped service into a component if you intend the service lifetime to match the lifetime of the component.
- BLZ-020: During client-side rendering (CSR, InteractiveWebAssembly), state persisted during prerendering is exposed to the browser and must not contain sensitive, private information. To improve the user experience, begin by implementing streaming rendering, to avoid waiting for an asynchronous task to complete while prerendering.
